question.knowledge_point: Finding Differences of Sets Given Verbally
question.problem: Let $C$  be the set of all multiples of $10$ greater than $0$ and let $D$  be the the set of all multiples of $5$ greater than $0.$ What is $C∖D?$
question.worked_solution:
The multiples of $10$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
C={10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D={5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & ={10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…}-{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form using the standard algorithm for Gaussian elimination, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -8 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & -7 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Reducing a 2x2 Augmented Matrix to REF Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & -1 & 11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y=8 \\  & y=-11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-11$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(-11)=8\,⇒\,x=8+11=19.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=19$ and $y=-11.$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=6 \\  & 4x-7y=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 6 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 4 & -7 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y=3 \\  & y=-2,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-2)=3\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=-2.$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-2y=4 \\  & 2x-y=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Writing a Function Using Arrow Notation
question.problem:
Which of the following is the correct symbolic notation for the sentence given below?

*"The function $f$ maps the set of real numbers to the set $Y.$"*
question.worked_solution:
The sentence *"The function $f$ maps the set of real numbers to the set $Y$"* is equivalent to the following symbolic notation:

$\,$ $f:R\to Y$

Here, the domain of $f$ is $R,$ and the codomain of $f$ is $Y.$

question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $g(x)=x-3{x}^{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
The notation $g(x)=x-3{x}^{2}$ means that the function $g$ maps the element $x$ in the domain to $x-3{x}^{2}$ in the codomain. This can also be written as

$$
g:x↦x-3{x}^{2}.
$$

$$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=8 \\  & -2x+2y-3z=-11 \\  & x+z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z=8 \\ y-z=1 \\ z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5)=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5)=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Matrix Form
question.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=au+bv+3,\,y=-9u+cv+4
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -9 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -9 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u \\ -9u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+3 \\ -9u+4v+4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x=1u+0v+3,\,y=-9u+4v+4
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=1+0+4=5.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Matrix Form
question.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=au+bv-2,\,y=u+c
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6u+8v \\ u\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6u+8v-2 \\ u+5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x=6u+8v-2,\,y=u+5
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=6+8+5=19.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Parametric Form
question.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=-5v-2,\,y=7v-2u-3
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & a \\ -2 & b\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}c \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

First, notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5v-2 \\ 7v-2u-3\end{aligned}].
$$

Separating the constants and expressing the linear part as a product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5v-2 \\ 7v-2u-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5v \\ -2u+7v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-5+7+(-2)=0.
$$
